description: Migration fixtures from current Sync .sync/ format. Each record is a generic Envelope that maps directly to Git Memory's envelope model.

records.title: Use MCP as the public seam between Sync and Git Memory
records.content: We chose MCP as the public contract because it is a language-agnostic JSON-RPC protocol that any consumer can speak. Sync and other clients depend on the MCP interface, not on private Rust crates. This allows independent versioning and release cycles.

extensions.rationale_summary: MCP is the language-agnostic public contract

records.title: Consumers must not depend on private Git Memory crates
records.content: Consumers (Sync, third-party tools) must use only the public MCP JSON-RPC interface. They must not add path dependencies on git-memory-store, git-memory-core, or other private crates. This ensures independent release cycles and compatibility guarantees.

records.title: Release artifacts, compatibility matrix and independent consumer
records.content: Final capstone spec. Proves Git Memory is a standalone product, not path dependencies that happen to compile next to Sync. Ships public contract, artifacts, fixtures and compatibility guarantees.

records.title: git-memory-contract crate already provides black-box behavioral tests
records.content: The git-memory-contract crate ships 9 scenarios: atomic_batch, snapshot_consistency, different_key_race, same_key_conflict, interrupted_write_recovery, history_diff_import_export, search_fts_and_filters, search_pagination, backlinks_explicit_and_mentions. ReleaseBinaryTarget launches the binary via stdio and validates the full MCP lifecycle.

records.title: Should model fingerprint changes trigger a re-index?
records.content: When the embedding model changes, vector distances become incomparable. Should the server automatically re-index, or should consumers decide? Current design: server reports modelFingerprint in handshake, consumers decide.
